fields.h1: Build a MaxDiff Survey With Best and Worst Picks
fields.hero_description: Build a MaxDiff survey that asks for a best and worst pick on each screen and scores every item in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Parts of a MaxDiff Survey Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the screens people answer and the scoring behind them from one prompt, and a later prompt changes either one.
fields.feature_1:
A best and a worst pick on each screen

Each screen shows a few items, such as 4 of your 20 features. The respondent marks one as most important and one as least, and the next screen opens once both are marked.
fields.feature_2:
Item sets that rotate evenly

Tell Emergent how many items go on each screen and how often each should appear, such as 3 times. The survey rotates sets so every item appears equally and none always sits first.
fields.feature_3:
One score for every item

The dashboard counts how often each item was picked best and worst out of the times it was shown. Best share minus worst share gives each item one score, and the leader comes first.
fields.feature_4:
Scores split by segment

Every pick is a row in a database you own, tagged with the respondent's segment, such as plan or region. Compare how free and paid users score one feature on the same dashboard.
fields.feature_5:
A Slack post or an email on a result

Ask for a Slack post or an email when a score crosses a line you set, such as a dish falling below -20. Emergent puts no cap on how many people answer each survey you run.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain and your own code

Put the survey on a custom domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and rerun the study later.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams Ranking Long Lists With MaxDiff
fields.tab_content_1:
Offline mode scores +37 to lead the roadmap

Taskwren had 16 features on its roadmap. The project management app shows 420 users 4 features per question over 12 questions, so each feature appears 3 times. Offline mode scores +37, dark mode lands at -26, and the team builds offline mode first.
fields.tab_content_2:
Fragrance free beats every other claim for the front label

Larchmint Skincare had 10 claims for the front of its new moisturizer jar. It asks 600 shoppers to pick the most and least convincing of 5 claims per question, over 6 questions. The results post to the #brand-team channel in Slack, and fragrance free, at +41, goes on the label.
fields.tab_content_3:
Nine screens decide which topic gets the main hall

Sundergate Summit asks 350 registered attendees to rank 12 session topics on their phones. Each screen shows 4 topics with a most wanted and a least wanted button, and 9 screens show every topic 3 times. Pricing workshops score +44 and get the main hall.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any dish under -20 goes to the head chef

Pennacombe Kitchens asks 480 loyalty members about 15 dishes before it rewrites the spring menu, 5 dishes per question over 9 questions. Any dish that scores below -20 is flagged, and the head chef gets an email listing them. Lamb tagine at -24 and veal liver at -41 come off the menu.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a MaxDiff Survey
fields.howto_description: Size a MaxDiff survey so each item is seen 3 times, build it with Emergent, and read every score in 7 steps.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List the items in plain words
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the decision the ranking will settle, such as which 2 features to build this quarter or which claim goes on the label. A MaxDiff survey ranks a list against itself. It cannot tell you whether anything on the list is worth doing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List every item in plain words of similar length, one idea per item. Sawtooth Software puts a MaxDiff exercise at about 15 to 40 items. Cut duplicates and anything you would never act on, because every extra item adds questions.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Show 4 or 5 items in each question, the subset size Sawtooth Software describes. A larger set means fewer questions but harder choices, and people start to skim. Keep each set below half of your list.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Multiply your item count by 3 and divide by the items per question. With 20 items and 4 per question, that is 15 questions. Sawtooth Software's calculator asks for enough questions to show each item 3 times to a respondent.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the list, the set size, and the question count in one prompt. Emergent builds the survey, the rotation, the database, and the scoring dashboard. A follow-up prompt adds a segment question, such as plan type or region.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Take it on a phone first
fields.howto_step_6_des: Answer the survey yourself on a phone before anyone else sees it. Check that every item fits on one line, that the most and least buttons sit side by side, and that a screen moves on only after both picks.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read each score as the share of showings in which an item was picked best, minus the share in which it was picked worst. Sawtooth Software calls this a quick summary score. A score near 0 means few picks either way, or an even split.

faq_plan.a: A MaxDiff survey shows a few items at a time and asks each person to pick the best and the worst in every set. Qualtrics describes the method as survey takers indicating the best and worst options out of a given set. After enough sets, every item has a score, and the scores put the whole list in order.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a maxdiff survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the items, how many to show per question and how many questions to ask, and Emergent's AI survey builder builds the survey, its rotation, and the scoring dashboard from that prompt. Answers are saved to a database you own, and you can change the item list later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: How are scores calculated in a MaxDiff survey?
faq_plan.a: There are two common scores. The quick one subtracts an item's worst-pick rate from its best-pick rate. Sawtooth Software also rescales scores to sum to 100 on a ratio scale, where an item scoring 10 is twice as preferred as one scoring 5. Emergent builds either score into the dashboard you ask for.

faq_plan.q: What kinds of lists work in a MaxDiff survey?
faq_plan.a: Any list where every item is a real option and you can act on only a few: features, packaging claims, session topics, menu dishes, benefits, or messages. Keep the items parallel: each should read as the same kind of choice. To learn who is answering, add a few audience survey questions after the MaxDiff screens.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should each person answer in a MaxDiff survey?
faq_plan.a: Between eight and fifteen, the range Sawtooth Software reports for one respondent. If your list needs more than that for 3 showings per item, trim the list or show more items per question. A 40-item list at 5 per question needs 24 questions, too many for one sitting.

faq_plan.q: When is a MaxDiff survey better than a rating scale?
faq_plan.a: When every item would rate high on a 1 to 5 scale and you need an order. Sawtooth Software notes that MaxDiff scores demonstrate greater discrimination among items. Use a rating scale when you need each item's absolute level, such as satisfaction with a service you already run.

faq_plan.q: Can I add other question types to a MaxDiff survey?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put screening and segment questions before the MaxDiff screens and open questions after them. The choices then come while attention is fresh. An airline ranking 12 cabin perks could follow up with airline survey questions about the respondent's last flight. Every answer type lands in the same database you own.

faq_plan.q: What does a negative score mean in a MaxDiff survey?
faq_plan.a: It means the item was picked worst more often than best across the times it was shown. A score of -26 says people actively reject the item, a stronger signal than a score near 0, which can mean indifference. Treat negative items as candidates to drop from the list.

faq_plan.q: Can a MaxDiff survey compare scores between customer groups?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Tag each answer with the group, such as free or paid plan, and compare each item's score group by group. Read small groups with care, because a few changed answers move a score from 30 people more than one from 300. With no response cap in Emergent, a small group can keep collecting answers.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a MaxDiff survey to set a meeting agenda?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when there are more candidate topics than time. List 8 to 12 topics, show 4 per question, and give the top scorers the most minutes. After the meeting, a short set of post meeting survey questions shows whether the chosen topics were worth the time.
